correctness.rationale: Chain-ring layers have sizes determined by the residue-field order; ideal-based vertices are exactly the s lifts of each nonzero zero-divisor coset. The lifted nonzero socle is precisely the universal set U, and for length at least three any valuation-one lift has neighborhood U. Hence a subset is total dominating iff it has at least two vertices and meets U. Counting gives the polynomial; minimum paired sets are exactly the two-vertex total sets. Direct ring computations replay all boundary cases used in the statement.

value.rationale: The result completely enumerates total dominating sets in a natural algebraic graph family and exposes fibre-size information invisible to the known minimum number. It also classifies/counts all minimum paired sets and handles the isolated boundary exactly. This is a motivated structural upgrade of a known parameter equality rather than a single recomputation.
